expectations.text: Requires ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, explaining that the table owner otherwise bypasses RLS entirely
expectations.evidence: "Without `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, the table owner skips every policy."

expectations.text: Rejects deriving app.tenant_id from the client-supplied X-Org-Id header and requires tenant identity injected server-side from a verified token
expectations.evidence: "The `X-Org-Id` header is client-supplied... Derive the tenant from the verified token claims."

expectations.text: Requires WITH CHECK alongside USING on write-path policies, because USING filters only reads and a USING-only policy lets a tenant write rows attributed to another tenant
expectations.evidence: WITH CHECK is listed under "Checked and fine" as mattering only if policies are split later; it is not required.

expectations.text: Warns that multiple permissive policies on a table combine with OR, so a single USING (true) policy silently defeats every stricter policy, and requires auditing all of a table's policies together
expectations.evidence: Only says to scope the policy `TO customers` so the API policy "can never OR-combine"; no USING (true) warning or audit requirement.

expectations.text: Requires WITH (security_invoker = true) on the four reporting views, since a view otherwise runs with its creator's privileges and returns every row regardless of caller
expectations.evidence: "create each view with `WITH (security_invoker = true)`."

expectations.text: Warns about infinite policy recursion when a helper function called from a policy reads another RLS-protected table, and prescribes SECURITY DEFINER with SET search_path pinned
expectations.evidence: Recursion note on helper functions that read other RLS tables; function uses `SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp`.

expectations.text: Recommends wrapping a per-row function call in a subquery so the predicate evaluates once per query rather than once per row
expectations.evidence: "Wrap any per-row function in `(SELECT …)`."

expectations.text: Requires indexing every column a policy predicate references, tenant_id first
expectations.evidence: "Index `tenant_id` as the leading column."

expectations.text: States that RLS does not itself grant SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, so matching GRANTs and column grants are still required
expectations.evidence: Never states that RLS needs matching GRANTs.

expectations.text: Rejects schema-per-tenant at roughly 900 tenants, naming connection pooling and DDL migrations as what breaks down
expectations.evidence: Names 900 DDL runs, catalog size, pg_dump and autovacuum, but not connection pooling.

expectations.text: States that an OLTP-only stack with no warehouse deletes the zero-copy sharing rung entirely rather than demoting it
expectations.evidence: "With no warehouse in your stack, zero-copy sharing isn't an option."

expectations.text: Rejects exposing the live operational schema to customers and requires a curated mart layer replicated from the system of record
expectations.evidence: "Publish a curated, versioned schema (`customer_api`, with `v1` views)".
